changes.before: Implement pair so both items survive in input order.
changes.after: Pair items from different sources when their item types match.

before: An associated type is a type slot declared by a protocol. Each conforming type supplies what that slot means. Two different conforming types can share the same item type.

ItemSource requires a readable item and names its type Item. Box<Value> infers Item from its stored item: Value. The automatically supplied Box(item:) initializer stores its argument. CountSource is a different conforming struct whose item is always Int; CountSource(item:) stores that Int. Box<Int> and CountSource are different source types with the same Item. pair accepts two possibly different source types A and B, but where A.Item == B.Item requires the same associated type, not equal item values. It returns an array containing the first then second item. [A.Item] is an array type whose element type is that shared item type.
Optional practice: Implement pair so both items survive in input order. Predict a different input before running.
after: A protocol can leave a place for a type using associatedtype. ItemSource calls that type Item. Any type that follows this protocol must provide a readable item of its chosen Item type.
Box<Value> stores an item of Value, so that becomes its Item type. CountSource always stores an Int item. These are different source types, but both can supply Int values.
pair accepts source types A and B. where A.Item == B.Item requires their item types to match. [A.Item] means the answer is an array of that shared item type.
The rule compares types, not values. The numbers 6 and 9 may differ and still be Int values. A number and text containing the same digit have different types, so they do not satisfy this rule.
Complete pair to return both items in order: a.item first, then b.item. Keep the rule requiring matching item types. Do not convert or replace either item.
